messages:
Nina: Paging: network alarms -- elevated TCP retransmits and timeouts observed for several customer sessions originating from eu-west-1a. Majority of failures are v6 paths; a lot of clients appear to fall back to v4 with high latency. Ticketing now. @incident-bot please page oncall.
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Incident created: #NET-1763286400. Severity: P1. Affected region: eu-west-1a. Symptoms: high TCP retransmits, failed large responses, intermittent DNS failures for dual-stack endpoints. Pager -> Samir.
Samir: taking 1. pinging infra. any direct customer reports?
Nina: Support has a handful of support cases reporting slow API responses and partial failures to download large model artifacts. Correlating with infra metrics now.
Meera: looking at edge metrics: egress throughput fine but retransmits spiking on v6 to certain prefixes. Traceroute shows path MTU issues: icmp6 PTB seen sporadically then disappears.
Jordan: attaching tcpdump from a pod in eu-west-1a edge (filtered for ICMPv6 + tcp handshakes):

--- begin snippet ---
17:42:10.123456 IP6 fe80::1 > 2001:db8:abcd::2: ICMP6, packet too big, mtu 1280, length 1500
17:42:10.123789 IP6 2001:db8:abcd::2 > 2031:db8:ffff::7: TCP 443: Flags [S], seq 0, win 64240, options [mss 1460], length 0
17:42:10.124000 IP6 2001:db8:abcd::2 > 2031:db8:ffff::7: TCP 443: Flags [S], seq 0, win 64240, options [mss 1460], length 0
--- end snippet ---

Jordan: looks like server tries to send >1280 byte frames and remote router (or middlebox) responds with PTB 1280. but many clients never get PTB, so they keep sending large segments -> blackhole. classic PMTUD failure for IPv6.
Samir: do we have recent change in transit (jumbo frames / overlay) in eu-west-1a? any router upgrades?
Kevin: infra change log shows a maintenance window last night for backbone routers in eu-west-1a where jumbo frame support was toggled to test throughput with partner. Ops note said 'do not enable on dualstack prefixes' but looks like some routes received modified MTU. Rolling back now.
Alex: while we rollback, we need a live mitigation. For IPv4 we get ICMP PTB reliably, but for v6 it's flaky. We can apply an MSS clamp for tcp SYN on the edge egress so we avoid path MTU >1280. For ipv6 we need ip6tables mangle TCPMSS. Proposed command for edge boxes (validate on canary first):

sudo ip6tables -t mangle -A POSTROUTING -p tcp --tcp-flags SYN,RST SYN -j TCPMSS --clamp-mss-to-pmtu

Meera: can confirm: applying TCPMSS on the egress NAT will reduce advertised MSS in SYN to ~1220 and avoid fragmentation issues. Good transient mitigation.
Samir: who can push this to the edge fleet now? Need to target eu-west-1a first. I will patch the control plane to push a single box in canary.
Jordan: note: ip6tables TCPMSS is kernel module dependent; some of our older AMIs need xt_TCPMSS. I'll patch one canary with module + ip6tables rule.
Samir: Alex, Meera, Jordan - roll?
Alex: rolling to canary now (eu-west-1a-edge-01). applying rule and monitoring healthchecks.
Support-Bot: notifying support rotation and customer success: customers with open cases in eu-west1 marked impacted. Suggested message draft prepared for CS.
Samir: can we also advertise temporary route shift to eu-west-1b for hostnames behind our routed load-balancer? That will be slower to failover but reduces blast radius. Ops: how long to shift traffic?
Kevin: we can shift subset of traffic via traffic-split for LB within 5-10 minutes. Doing 10% -> 50% -> 100% if canary looks good.
Meera: canary results: after TCPMSS applied, SYN from remote had MSS 1220, connections completed, retransmit rate dropped ~85% on that box.
Samir: proceed with 10% shift to eu-west-1b while we continue clamp rollout and rollback router jumbo-flag.
Jordan: also seeing intermittent DNS NXDOMAINs from resolver upstream when v6 path fails; suspect split-horizon between v4 and v6 resolvers in that AZ. We should inform DNS partners.
Nina: drafting customer-facing status: "We are investigating connectivity degradation for some EU customers. Mitigation in progress; engineering has applied temporary MTU clamp to edge nodes in eu-west-1a and is shifting traffic. We'll update in 15m." Any objections? :thumbsup:/thumbsdown
Alex: :thumbsup:
Kevin: :thumbsup:
Samir: :thumbsup:

--- 30 minutes later ---
Meera: rollback of jumbo-flags on backbone routers in eu-west-1a completed at 1763286900. No config drift observed now. Continued TCPMSS clamp on edges for 30m to be safe.
Jordan: monitoring: v6 retransmits down to baseline, API latencies back to normal for affected customers. DNS NXDOMAINs cleared after traffic shift.
Support-Bot: support notified customers in affected cases with status update. CS asked for timeline; we've given 2h followup.
Samir: marking action items: (1) keep TCPMSS clamp for 30m, then remove and verify. (2) postmortem to track why router change was applied to dual-stack prefixes. (3) add automated MTU-change guard in deployment pipeline. (4) Run BGP/route tests to detect MTU mismatches proactively.
Nina: resolution timeline: mitigation deployed 1763286640, backbone rollback completed 1763286900, monitoring confirms recovery at 1763286960. I'll create incident doc and assign postmortem to Meera + Kevin.
Alex: quick note: consider enabling PMTUD probes visibility in our synthetic checks for both v4 and v6, and add icmp6-ptb counts to console.
Samir: thanks team. I'm handing off to morning shift for followup. Samir out.
incident-bot: Incident #NET-1763286400 status -> mitigated. Postmortem requested.
Nina: thanks everyone. We'll keep the postmortem brief and include clear remediation steps so this doesn't reoccur."
